news.title: Apple Unveils AI-Powered Smart Glasses at WWDC 2026
news.content:
Apple announced its long-awaited smart glasses at the Worldwide Developers Conference on Monday, marking the company's boldest push into wearable artificial intelligence. The device, called Apple Vision Lite, weighs just 45 grams and features a transparent micro-OLED display that overlays digital information onto the real world.

Unlike the bulky Vision Pro headset released in 2024, the new glasses resemble ordinary eyewear and can be worn comfortably throughout the day. The built-in AI assistant can identify objects, translate languages in real time, and provide navigation directions directly in the user's field of vision.

The glasses are powered by a custom M5 chip designed specifically for on-device AI processing. This means most computations happen locally, reducing latency and addressing privacy concerns. Apple emphasized that no images or conversations are sent to the cloud without explicit user permission.

Battery life reaches approximately eight hours with moderate use, and the glasses charge wirelessly through a compact carrying case. Third-party developers can build applications using the new visionOS Lite SDK, which supports gesture recognition and voice commands.

Industry analysts predict the device could sell over 30 million units in its first year, potentially creating a new product category that bridges the gap between smartphones and augmented reality. Pre-orders begin next month at a starting price of 799 dollars, significantly lower than the Vision Pro's launch price.
